baselines: Naive empty baseline: submission/vulnerability_report.json with suspect_nets=[], algebraic_masking_correct=false, vulnerability_summary='', hardening_proposal={registers_to_add:[], placement_description:''}, confidence=0.0 -- must FAIL all SRs and most FRs.

metrics.description: Binary/graded score for whether the report correctly attributes leakage to glitch propagation through unregistered combinational recombination rather than an algebraic masking defect, per SR1.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Fraction of the ground-truth glitch-sensitive nets (and_cross0, and_cross1, and the XOR recombination point) correctly named in suspect_nets, per SR2.
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Correctness of the proposed register placement relative to the true recombination boundary, penalizing proposals that register only final outputs or unrelated signals, per SR3.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

metrics.description: Whether submission/vulnerability_report.json satisfies the required field presence, types, and formatting per FR1-FR4.
metrics.name: schema_conformance

acceptance_criteria: A submission scoring PASS must set algebraic_masking_correct=true, list both and_cross0 and and_cross1 (or file-verified equivalents) in suspect_nets, describe the glitch/timing mechanism substantively (not just algebraic correctness) in vulnerability_summary, and propose registers on the internal cross/same-term nets (or equivalently on all four input shares plus mask) prior to the XOR recombination stage.
The baseline/naive empty submission (missing fields, or suspect_nets=[], or algebraic_masking_correct=false, or hardening_proposal registering only the final q0/q1 outputs) must FAIL.

Optional cross-check: evaluate.py may run iverilog/vvp on inputs/masked_and.v using stimulus derived from inputs/sim_trace.vcd.txt to confirm q0^q1 matches (a0^a1)&(b0^b1) for all sampled vectors, corroborating SR1's algebraic-correctness claim independent of the submitted report.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The masked_and module computes q0 and q1 combinationally from a0,a1,b0,b1 and a fresh random mask bit r using the standard first-order Boolean masking formula for AND (e.g. q0 = (a0&b0) ^ r, q1 = (a1&b1) ^ ((a0&b1) ^ (a1&b0) ^ r)). Algebraically this is correct: q0^q1 == (a0^a1)&(b0^b1) always holds. However, the module has no internal pipeline registers between the four input shares and the output shares -- all cross-share AND terms (named internally as and_cross0 = a0&b1 and and_cross1 = a1&b0) and the same-share terms (and_same0 = a0&b0, and_same1 = a1&b1) are combined by a single XOR tree in the same combinational cycle. Because a0,a1,b0,b1 do not all arrive at the gates simultaneously in real silicon (different fan-in depths, wire delays, glitches from upstream logic), the intermediate nets and_cross0 and and_cross1 -- and the XOR combination point where and_same0/and_same1/and_cross0/and_cross1/r are merged -- experience transient glitches during which signals derived from BOTH shares of an operand are momentarily present on the same node before settling. This transient joint dependency on (a0,a1) or (b0,b1) together defeats the first-order independence property that masking relies on, even though the final settled value is masked correctly. The fix is to insert registers on the share-domain intermediate signals (specifically registering and_same0, and_same1, and_cross0, and_cross1, and the mask r before they are combined by the final XOR stage, or equivalently registering a0,a1,b0,b1,r at the gadget's input boundary and again registering q0,q1 at the output) so that no combinational glitch path spans both shares of an operand within a single clock cycle. This restores the first-order non-completeness/glitch-robustness property.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check 'algebraic_masking_correct' == true AND that 'vulnerability_summary' text contains concepts matching glitch/transient/timing/unregistered combinational recombination (keyword and semantic matching against ground_truth mechanism), rejecting reports that claim the masking scheme itself is mathematically wrong.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify that the leakage source is glitch propagation through unregistered combinational recombination logic, not an algebraic masking flaw.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Verify 'suspect_nets' includes at least the two cross-term nets (matched against ground-truth identifiers and_cross0/and_cross1, allowing for reasonable naming variants confirmed by tracing the actual assign statements in inputs/masked_and.v) and optionally the XOR recombination node; partial credit if only one of the two cross terms is found, full credit requires both plus the shared combination point or an equivalent complete explanation.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must name the specific glitch-sensitive intermediate nets that combine shares of both operands within a single unregistered combinational stage.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse 'hardening_proposal.registers_to_add' and 'placement_description'; confirm the named signals correspond (by tracing the netlist dataflow graph derived from inputs/masked_and.v) to points upstream of or at the final XOR combination of and_same0/and_same1/and_cross0/and_cross1/r, i.e. registering happens strictly before the single-cycle combinational path that spans both shares completes; reject proposals that only register the final output q0/q1 without addressing the internal cross-share combination, since that leaves the same single-cycle glitch path intact upstream of the new register.
security_requirements.requirement: The hardening proposal must correctly place new registers so that share-domain values are latched before being combined across the cross-term/same-term XOR stage, restoring cycle-by-cycle non-completeness.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker with physical or simulated access to power/EM side-channel traces of the hardware implementing this gadget observes glitch-induced transient activity on internal combinational nodes. Even though the masking scheme is algebraically sound at steady state, unregistered combinational recombination of cross-share and same-share partial products causes both shares of an operand to transiently influence a single node's switching activity within one clock cycle, producing a first-order-exploitable leakage in a glitch-extended probing/power model (e.g. the glitch-extended probing model of Faust et al. / robust probing model). The attacker does not need multivariate statistics; univariate CPA/DPA on the recombination node's transient activity suffices to recover the unmasked secret bit correlation.

constraints: The RTL module masked_and must implement a first-order Boolean masking scheme for AND that is algebraically correct: q0 XOR q1 always equals (a0 XOR a1) AND (b0 XOR b1) for all input combinations, when evaluated at steady state (ignoring transient glitches).

The masked_and gadget must be implemented as pure combinational logic (no internal registers) between the input share ports and the output share ports, so that any leakage is caused purely by glitch propagation through unregistered combinational logic rather than by an algebraic masking error.
All input artifacts must be self-contained plain text files (Verilog-2001 compatible, parseable by iverilog) requiring no external IP or proprietary libraries.
The design_brief.md must describe the module's intended function and port list in purely functional terms without naming any security weakness, CWE identifier, or vulnerability category.

sim_trace.vcd.txt must be a plain-text, human-readable representation of a value-change dump (or an equivalent stimulus/response table) sufficient to let evaluate.py reconstruct or re-run the same stimulus via iverilog/vvp.
expected_outputs: submission/vulnerability_report.json containing named suspect nets, an architectural explanation, and a hardening proposal with register placement

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/vulnerability_report.json must be syntactically valid JSON and contain all five required top-level fields (suspect_nets, algebraic_masking_correct, vulnerability_summary, hardening_proposal, confidence) with the exact types specified in the interface.

Every string listed in 'suspect_nets' must correspond to an actual wire/reg declared or assigned in inputs/masked_and.v (verifiable by simple text/AST search); submissions listing zero nets or fabricated names not present in the file fail this requirement.

'algebraic_masking_correct' must be set to true, consistent with the fact that the provided gadget is algebraically correct (q0 XOR q1 equals the correct AND) under static evaluation, as verifiable by simulating inputs/masked_and.v with iverilog/vvp over the vectors implied by inputs/sim_trace.vcd.txt.

'hardening_proposal.registers_to_add' must be non-empty and each entry must name a signal that lies on the dataflow path between the identified suspect nets and the module's output ports q0/q1, as determined by tracing inputs/masked_and.v's assign/always statements.

public_spec.interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json (UTF-8, valid JSON, no trailing commentary). It MUST contain top-level fields: (1) 'suspect_nets': array of strings, each an exact net/wire identifier as it appears in inputs/masked_and.v (e.g. 'and_cross0'); (2) 'algebraic_masking_correct': boolean, your assessment of whether q0 XOR q1 equals the correct AND of the unmasked operands under static (non-glitch) evaluation; (3) 'vulnerability_summary': string (>=40 characters) describing the mechanism by which the identified nets create a security weakness; (4) 'hardening_proposal': object with fields 'registers_to_add': array of strings naming the exact signal(s) that should be registered (each string must reference a net name that exists in inputs/masked_and.v or a clearly derived share-domain equivalent name), and 'placement_description': string (>=40 characters) explaining where in the dataflow (before/after which combinational stage) the new registers go and why that restores independence; (5) 'confidence': number between 0.0 and 1.0. evaluate.py reads inputs/masked_and.v, inputs/fault_model.json, and optionally uses iverilog/vvp to re-simulate inputs/masked_and.v against inputs/sim_trace.vcd.txt to cross-check any claimed toggling behavior, then grades submission/vulnerability_report.json against hidden ground truth for field presence, format, and substantive correctness.
public_spec.objective: A hardware team has implemented a first-order Boolean-masked AND gadget (Verilog module masked_and) intended to combine two secret-shared operands (a0,a1) and (b0,b1) into an output shared as (q0,q1), such that q0 XOR q1 == (a0 XOR a1) AND (b0 XOR b1). Review the provided RTL and its testbench-derived simulation trace, then produce a structured engineering report that documents the internal signal structure of the gadget: which internal nets carry which partial products, how those nets are combined, and where registers exist (or do not exist) in the signal path between combinational blocks. Your report must also propose a concrete RTL restructuring (register placement) that you believe improves the gadget's resistance to unintended timing-dependent recombination effects, and justify why the proposed placement changes the timing/ordering of signal arrivals at the recombination point.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json matching the schema described in public_spec.interface. No additional files are graded.

title: Glitch-induced unmasking in a combinational masked AND
